title: Akshay Kumar Walks Back Into the 'Welcome' Jungle Tonight — but the Advance Booking Is Whispering, Not Roaring
excerpt: Paid previews kick off at 7:30 PM with the franchise's biggest-ever ensemble, yet pre-sales are trailing 'Bhooth Bangla'. The third 'Welcome' is betting everything on a Muharram holiday and word of mouth.
body:
By the time you read this, the doors are already open. At 7:30 PM tonight, across PVR Inox and Cinepolis screens from Mumbai to Edison, New Jersey, Welcome To The Jungle begins its paid previews — and Akshay Kumar strides back into the chaos franchise that turned 'control uncontrol' into a national catchphrase.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=R704yP3dlXw https://x.com/akshaykumar/status/2070364268747424044

The cast list alone reads like a wedding guest book that got out of hand: Akshay Kumar, Suniel Shetty, Paresh Rawal, Arshad Warsi, Disha Patani, Jacqueline Fernandez, Lara Dutta, Raveena Tandon, Johnny Lever, Rajpal Yadav, Krishna Abhishek and a small army of others, all corralled by director Ahmed Khan into a jungle setting built for maximum slapstick mayhem. It is, by ticket count of names on the poster, one of the biggest ensembles a Bollywood comedy has ever attempted.

The nostalgia bait is real. Raveena Tandon sharing frames with Akshay again — twenty-two years after Mohra — is the kind of reunion that makes the front benches roar. The Welcome series has a fiercely loyal audience that shows up for the gags, the over-the-top villains and the sheer scale of it all.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZ_6FzYNoZ3/

And yet — here's where the spectacle meets the spreadsheet — the numbers are murmuring rather than thundering.

As of Thursday morning, the film had sold roughly 20,000 tickets across the top national chains for opening day plus paid previews. That's a decent figure on its own, but context bites: it's tracking about 20 percent lower than Akshay's last release, the horror-comedy Bhooth Bangla, which closed advances near 72,000 tickets. Trade forecasters at Pinkvilla peg the opening in the ₹13–17 crore range, with the paid previews padding the Friday haul.

The diagnosis from the trade is blunt and a little brutal: the promos sold a spoof rather than a family entertainer, and a franchise with this much IP value should be doing far better at this stage. The marketing, the argument goes, leaned slapstick when it should have leaned event.

But the film has two cards left to play. The first is Muharram, a public holiday on Friday across much of India, which historically fattens walk-in business and gives a soft opener room to breathe. The second — the oldest card in the Bollywood deck — is word of mouth. The entire paid-preview strategy exists for exactly this: get bodies into seats tonight, let the laughs travel, and convert a sluggish advance into a healthy Friday. A film like this lives or dies on whether aunties text their group chats "timepass hai, jaa sakte ho" by Friday morning.

For the diaspora, Welcome To The Jungle is a near-guaranteed theatrical release in the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf — the Welcome films are reliable overseas earners, the comfort-food comedy that pulls family audiences out on a Friday night and packs the desi-heavy multiplexes in New Jersey, Toronto and the Bay Area. Overseas previews typically run in step with India, so North American fans can catch it this weekend. A streaming window, likely on Prime Video or Netflix, usually follows a big-comedy theatrical run within roughly eight weeks.

The CBFC handed the film a U/A 16+ and a hefty 2-hour-44-minute runtime, trimming a few dialogues along the way — the usual pre-release haircut.

Here's the honest take: on paper, this should be a slam dunk — a beloved franchise, a stacked cast, a holiday weekend, an Akshay Kumar riding a hot streak. The advance says the audience isn't fully convinced yet. The previews tonight are the film's chance to change their minds. Comedies are the genre most likely to outrun a weak start on pure momentum, and if any title is built to do that, it's a Welcome. By Saturday we'll know whether the jungle still roars — or whether the third time around, the joke is wearing thin.
